inputs_state_output: These sources are estimators, not trackers. Mapping of their roles: the 'strong base' is the conditioning variable B in [2] (baseline representation, e.g. ELMo/RoBERTa layer 0) or X1 in [4]; the 'added branch' is phi(X) in [2] / X in [3] / X2 in [4]. Inputs: fixed, already computed representations, a label Y and a chosen predictive family V (probe). There is no internal state or memory; the output is a number in bits: V-entropy H_V(Y|.) = inf_{f in V} E[-log2 f[.](Y)] estimated as held-out cross-entropy ([3] eq. 1-2), V-information I_V(X->Y) = H_V(Y) - H_V(Y|X) ([3] eq. 3), conditional V-information I_V(X->Y|B) = H_V(Y|B) - H_V(Y|B,X) ([3] eq. 6, from [2]), pointwise PVI(x->y) = -log2 g[null](y) + log2 g'[x](y) ([3] eq. 4) and PID terms R, U1, U2, S ([4] eq. 1-3). Ours: B = appearance block of the hybrid readout (frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign cosines to exemplar, previous target, bank, snapped-exemplar cosine, 32 PCA products, geometry, tag and within-query relative versions, as built in scripts/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026.py); X = FlyVis block (columns 8..237 of F1 in runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/train26_features_D.npz: 34 output types incl. T4/T5 regional activity plus 6-neighbour means and derived descriptors, plus 21 within-query relative fly keys); controls X' = same columns from the R1 (eye input) and C (stock) arrays. Y = ident per real detection region (train26: 5345 labelled rows, 928 positives, 4417 negatives; 3145 queries with labels, 1839 of them with a single labelled region, only 409 queries with a positive and at least one labelled negative - counted from train26_features_D.npz). Temporal state of FlyVis (exemplar + search frames) is already folded into the saved features; the estimators cannot see what the core state discarded.
fusion_and_training: [2]: two probes of the same family, one on the concatenation [B; phi(X)] and one on [B; 0] (or on B alone, footnote 3); conditional probing performance Perf([B;phi(X)]) - Perf([B;0]) with negative cross-entropy as Perf estimates I_V(phi(X)->Y|B) (Appendix B.3). Family in their experiments: affine + softmax, Adam lr 0.001 halved on plateau (section 4.1). Nothing is frozen except the representations; no alpha, gating or zero-init (those belong to C01). [3]: one model trained on the input and one 'null' model trained on an empty input to fit the label prior; both fine-tuned with cross-entropy; avoid overfitting because the held-out loss estimates the infimum (section 2.2); conditional variant by concatenating inputs (section 4.4). [4] BATCH: unimodal classifiers p(y|x1), p(y|x2) trained separately, then a network parameterising a joint q(x1,x2,y) normalised by unrolled Sinkhorn to match both unimodal marginals, maximising I_q(X1;X2;Y) (section 3.2) - structurally this is unimodal pre-training followed by a coupling stage. CVX: features histogrammed/clustered to a discrete support, convex optimisation over q in Delta_p (section 3.1). Implication for ours: the 'fusion' inside the estimator is whatever the probe family V can do. Our current measurement uses V = HistGradientBoosting on concatenated features; a zero or negative conditional V-information under this V does not exclude information usable by another fusion (V-information is family-dependent and can be created by computation, [1] section 3.2, violation of data processing). Therefore the precheck must use the SAME V for base and base+fly, and at least two families (regularised logistic and the frozen boosting configuration), and, if a learned projection with alpha (C01) is the intended deployment fusion, that family must also be in the probe set.
labels_and_loss: All sources use the log-likelihood (cross-entropy, bits) of the gold label as the information measure; V-information subtracts the null-model entropy H_V(Y), so it is not inflated by class imbalance the way accuracy is ([3] section 2.4: if X and Y are independent, V-information is provably zero whereas accuracy equals the majority rate). PVI is per-instance and can be negative even though V-information is non-negative ([3] section 3.1); [3] finds incorrectly predicted instances have lower PVI and the PVI at which predictions turn incorrect is about 0.5 bits across datasets (section 3.2, Fig. 3). No source treats hard negatives explicitly; slices of hard instances are handled by averaging PVI over the slice, which [3] stresses is NOT the V-information of the slice (section 3.1). For ours three label granularities are needed: (a) row level, binary ident per region (what the boosting predicts; prior entropy H_b(928/5345 = 0.174) = 0.666 bits/row on train26); (b) query level, categorical choice of the true region among the labelled candidates (softmax over candidate logits) - the quantity the identity stage actually decides; (c) pair level for confusable neighbours: target t vs nearest MASA-similar neighbour n, PVI_pair = log2 sigma(s_AF(t) - s_AF(n)) - log2 sigma(s_A(t) - s_A(n)). Imbalance (1:4.8 positives) is absorbed by the null entropy at row level; at query level the null is uniform over candidates.
data_camera_resolution_rate: No video or camera data in the sources. [2]: UD/PTB-style word-level tasks (upos, xpos, dependency labels), NER, SST-2 on ELMo and RoBERTa. [3]: SNLI, MultiNLI, CoLA, DWMW17 and others with BERT/RoBERTa/GPT-2-type models. [4]: synthetic generative datasets with known R/U/S, MultiBench (sentiment, humor, MIMIC, MuJoCo Push 1000 trajectories x 250 steps at 10 Hz, ENRICO, etc.), VQA 2.0, CLEVR, plus case studies (e.g. MAPS 844 samples from 17 participants). Sample sizes are mostly 10^3-10^6 i.i.d. instances. Ours: BDD100K train-split videos (fit104 = fit84 + fit20 for fitting/calibration, train26 for one evaluation), day/night, glare, occlusion; FlyVis sees a bounded grey crop; the effective sample for confidence intervals is the number of videos (26 clusters on train26), not the 5345 rows, because rows within a video are dependent.
metrics_and_numbers: [1] Theorem 1 (section 4): with |log f| <= B, with probability >= 1-2delta, |I_V - I_V_hat| <= 4 R_|D|(G_V) + 2B sqrt(2 log(1/delta)/|D|); Rademacher term typically O(|D|^-1/2). [2] Table 1 (ELMo, bits of V-information): upos baselined phi1 0.20 / phi2 0.16 vs conditional (given phi0) 0.22 / 0.20; dep rel 0.99/0.81 vs 1.00/0.87; sst2 0.18/0.13 vs 0.17/0.13 - conditioning changed the layer comparison (section 4.2, Fig. 1 for RoBERTa). [3] section 4.4: offensive words carry 0.482 bits of BERT-usable information about the label beyond sentiment vs 0.490 bits total (almost all unique); section 3.2: PVI about 0.5 bits is where predictions become incorrect (Fig. 3); Appendix A, Fig. 6: 80% of SNLI training data gives the same V-information estimate as 100% (plateau test of sample sufficiency); Appendix D Tables 5-6: cross-epoch/seed Pearson correlations of PVI roughly 0.75-0.95; section 3.2: cross-model PVI correlations lower on CoLA (0.40 < r < 0.65). [4] Table 2: CVX and BATCH agree on relative PID values on synthetic data with known interactions but assign non-zero synergy to datasets whose labels do not depend on synergy (label noise) - an estimator bias; case study 3 (MuJoCo Push): low U2 and high R predicted that a multimodal model would not beat unimodal ones, and no performance difference was observed; Conclusion: estimators only approximate interactions because of cluster pre-processing or unimodal classifiers. These are the authors' NLP/multimodal numbers and give no expectation for our identity AUC, utility or HOTA.
distinguishing_ablations: [2]: the key ablation is baselined probing (Perf(phi) - Perf(B)) versus conditional probing (Perf([B;phi]) - Perf([B;0])): baselined probing can show a 'negative' result for a representation that still contributes unique information, and conditioning on phi0 shrank the phi1-phi2 gap (Table 1) - i.e. 'strong alone' and 'useful beyond the base' are different quantities. Directly relevant: our FlyVis-alone AUC 0.950-0.956 says nothing about uniqueness; the conditional quantity is what matters. [3] section 4.4: conditioning out sentiment left 0.482 of 0.490 bits - an example where the added variable is almost fully unique; the method equally reports near-zero when it is redundant. [4]: synthetic datasets with ground-truth redundancy/uniqueness/synergy validate both estimators (Table 2); the robotics case shows a negative result (high R, low U2 -> no fusion gain) predicted beforehand. None of the sources runs an equal-capacity non-informative branch; [2] footnote 3 uses a constant placeholder. For us the equal-capacity null must be added explicitly: the fly block permuted across rows within each video (same dimension and marginals, link to Y broken) and the R1 and C blocks of equal dimension. No seeds/run variance is reported for conditional V-information differences in [2]; [3] reports PVI stability across seeds/epochs.
explanations_addressed: (1) Fly carries no unique identity information beyond appearance: DIRECT method - conditional V-information I_V(D->Y|A) and the FlyVis-specific I_V(D->Y|A,R1) with a permutation null; PID U_fly vs R. Our existing AUC numbers (train26 appearance 0.965, +D 0.973, +C 0.971, +R1 0.971; runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json -> identity) are a ranking analogue of this quantity and already suggest that whatever D adds over A is shared with R1 and C. (2) Information exists but fusion/training ignores it (modality imbalance): PARTIAL - V-information is family-dependent; computing it with two or three probe families (logistic, frozen boosting, boosting/MLP with explicit appearance-ambiguity interactions) separates 'no usable information for any tried family' from 'usable by a richer family'; a PID synergy term above null with U_fly near 0 indicates a moderation/gating role that concatenation into boosting may exploit poorly. A positive row-level gain with zero utility change points to decision-irrelevant information rather than imbalance. (3) Saved readout lost the information, new activity or fine-tuned core needed: CAUTION - estimators on saved features only bound what those features carry. Data processing (Shannon) means any fine-tuned FlyVis output has at most the information of the eye-input sequence it sees; V-usable information can be created by computation ([1] section 3.2), so fine-tuning can only make input information usable. The upper bound for core fine-tuning is therefore I_V'(eye-input sequence -> Y | A) with a flexible no-fly family V'; saved R1 summaries give only a weak proxy. (4) FlyVis lacks the lobula/LC identity pathway: NOT ADDRESSED directly; same logic as (3) - an added lobula-like layer is a function of the same input. (5) Gain only in subsets diluted by averaging: DIRECT tool - mean PVI per slice (darkness/glare by crop luminance, occlusion duration, small MASA cosine margin between target and nearest neighbour, crossing paths); [3] warns that slice-mean PVI is not slice V-information; with only 409 confusable queries on train26, slices hold tens to ~150 queries, so slice CIs will be wide. (6) Ceiling too low: ADDRESSED by conversion arithmetic, not by the sources - bits do not map monotonically to utility (Hellman-Raviv / Fano-type bounds [11] are loose); count-level gap on train26 (report.json -> counts): base helpful-harmful 137-98 = 39, base+D 129-84 = 45, perfect identity 321-154 = 167; the fly closed 6 of 128 net events (4.7%) of the identity gap; reaching +2 pp over the bench would need roughly 2/2.836 x 167 = 118 net events, about +79 over base (about 62% of the gap) [uncertain: proportional conversion ignores per-video normalisation].
evidence_strength: [1] ICLR 2020 peer-reviewed theory; [2] EMNLP 2021 peer-reviewed, code verified; [3] ICML 2022 Outstanding Paper, code verified; [4] NeurIPS 2023 peer-reviewed, code page reachable, estimators validated against ground truth only on synthetic data. [2]+[3] are one research line, not independent replications. Overall: STRONG as methodology for measuring conditional usable information with a fixed probe family; NO evidence about motion/bio features, tracking or FlyVis; PID estimators MODERATE (approximate, binning/unimodal-classifier dependent, spurious synergy under label noise).
difference_from_tried: Tried so far: AUC of the boosting readout with and without fly blocks and paired offline utility differences (base_D - base +0.409 [0.134; 0.687] on reused fit104; +0.106 [-0.176; +0.400] on train26; base_D - base_R1 -0.042; base_D - base_C -0.095; runs/z13_hybrid_identity_v2_20261026/internal_report.json and runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json). Not tried: (i) log-likelihood (bits) gain of the same probe with vs without fly, cross-fitted by video, with a permutation null of equal dimension; (ii) conditioning on R1 and C inside the information quantity (I(D->Y|A,R1)) instead of comparing utilities of separate arms; (iii) choice-level and confusable-pair PVI with flip counts; (iv) PID separation of unique vs synergistic fly information; (v) learning-curve test of sample sufficiency; (vi) an eye-input upper bound for core fine-tuning. This is a measurement, not a new fusion mechanism: it adds sensitivity (uses all row probabilities, not only gate firings) and attribution (unique vs shared with R1/C), but cannot by itself improve the bench.
math_precheck:
Goal: decide on CPU, before any GPU identity fine-tuning of the FlyVis core, whether FlyVis activity can add identity information beyond MASA appearance and beyond its own eye input, and whether any such information is large enough to matter for the +2 pp criterion. STEP 0 (data, CPU, no new FlyVis maps): rebuild the row matrices exactly as in scripts/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026.py (B = appearance block; D, C, R1 = F1[...,8:] + relative fly keys of each arm); labels ident; groups = video; splits: fit104 with 5-fold grouped cross-fitting (estimation), train26 with probes frozen from fit104 (confirmation). Record that fit104 was reused for selection and train26 has been evaluated once for this configuration; an untouched video set should be preferred for the confirmatory step if one exists [uncertain]. STEP 1 (row-level conditional V-information, [2][3]): for V = frozen HistGradientBoosting (same PROBE parameters) and V = L2 logistic regression, compute out-of-fold probabilities clipped to [1e-4, 1-1e-4], identically calibrated for every arm, and Ihat(D->Y|A) = mean_r[-log2 p_A(y_r) + log2 p_{A,D}(y_r)]; likewise Ihat(D->Y|A,R1), Ihat(D->Y|A,C), Ihat(R1->Y|A), Ihat(C->Y|A). Per-row gains d_r are paired PVI-style differences; CI by video cluster bootstrap (2000 resamples of videos, equal weight per video). Null: refit with the D block permuted within video 100-200 times; report Ihat minus the null 95th percentile (the null mean measures estimator bias from extra dimensions, usually negative for held-out loss). Bias/variance facts: held-out cross-entropy overestimates H_V (estimation error), more for the larger input, so Ihat(D|A) is conservatively biased when D is weak; selection over arms/hyperparameters on the same data biases it upward (cf. fit104 +0.409 vs train26 +0.106 pp). Xu et al. Theorem 1 is vacuous here: with clipping B = log2(1e4) = 13.3 bits, N = 5345, delta = 0.025, the deviation term alone 2B sqrt(2 ln(1/delta)/N) = 0.99 bits exceeds the prior entropy 0.666 bits, so only resampling CIs are usable. Sample size: SE is governed by 26 video clusters on train26; minimum detectable effect about 2.9 x sd_video(d_v)/sqrt(26) (80% power, two-sided 5%, t with 25 df); estimate sd_video on fit104 first. Sufficiency check ([3] Appendix A): recompute Ihat at 50/70/85/100% of training videos; a still-rising curve means data-limited -> inconclusive, not stop. kNN CMI estimators ([7][8]) and variational MI bounds ([10]) are not recommended as primary: 100-300 dimensions, few thousand rows and binary Y make the probe-difference (classifier-based, cf. [9]) estimator the natural one; CMIknn may be run only on 1-3 dimensional score summaries as a sanity check. STEP 2 (choice-level and pair-level PVI on confusable queries): on queries with >=2 labelled candidates and one positive (409 on train26), softmax the out-of-fold logits over candidates; PVI_q = log2 p_{A,D}(true|q) - log2 p_A(true|q); report mean PVI (bits/query) with video bootstrap, net flips n(wrong->right) - n(right->wrong) of the argmax with an exact McNemar test, and the same for A+R1 and A+C. Pair PVI against the nearest MASA-similar neighbour isolates the 'similar look' regime. Complementarity: among queries where the A-probe argmax is wrong, the rate at which a D-only probe is right versus an R1-only probe of equal dimension. Slice means of PVI by crop luminance, occlusion length and MASA cosine margin (label as slice-mean PVI, not V-information). STEP 3 (PID, [4][5]): x1 = quintile bin of out-of-fold appearance-only logit, x2 = quintile bin of fly-only logit (and separately of the fly logit residualised on R1), y binary; 5x5x2 = 50 cells. Plug-in bias of a joint MI is about (cells-1)/(2N ln2) = 0.0066 bits at N = 5345 (0.027 bits with 10 bins, i.e. comparable to plausible effects), so use 5 bins and a within-video shuffle null for U_fly and S. Read: U_fly and S at null with high R -> fly redundant with appearance; S above null with U_fly at null -> fly only informative jointly (moderation; gating fusion candidate); U_fly above null -> unique information. Score-level PID is a lower bound of feature-level quantities (scores are functions of features) and CVX on binned features underestimates high-dimensional uniqueness ([4] case study 3). STEP 4 (link to achievable gain): bits on rows the gate never touches do not change utility; restrict PVI to decision-relevant rows (base probability within the calibrated gate band, or queries where either arm's gate fires). Count conversion from runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json -> counts: identity gap = 167 - 39 = 128 net helpful events on train26; base+D closed 6 (4.7%); +2 pp over the bench needs about +79 net events over base (about 62% of the gap) [uncertain]. DECISION RULE (register before computing): PASS-A (FlyVis-specific usable information): lower 95% bound of Ihat(D->Y|A,R1) minus the permutation-null 95th percentile > 0 on fit104 cross-fit AND on the confirmation set, for at least one pre-declared family. PASS-B (decision relevance): net flips on confusable queries > 0 with McNemar p < 0.05 and lower bound of decision-band mean PVI > 0. PASS-C (headroom): the upper 95% bound of the projected net events gained by D over A+R1 reaches the ~79 needed for +2 pp; if not, fly identity alone cannot solve the problem even if PASS-A holds, and any FlyVis claim stays at '(fly+X) > (X)'. GPU core fine-tuning on identity is justified only if, in addition, a flexible no-fly model on the eye-input sequence shows Ihat(eye->Y|A) - Ihat(D->Y|A) > 0 with CI above 0 (unexploited input information that fine-tuning could make usable). STOP (no GPU identity training of the current fly input) if PASS-A fails with an MDE below the effect needed for PASS-C and the learning curve has plateaued; INCONCLUSIVE (collect more videos, still no GPU) if MDE exceeds the needed effect or the curve still rises. Code sketch (CPU): 
# CPU sketch (sklearn/numpy only). X_A, X_D, X_R: row blocks built exactly as in
# scripts/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026.py (B, fly F1[...,8:] + relative keys, R1 F1[...,8:]);
# y: ident in {0,1} for real labelled regions; vid: video id per row; qid: query uid per row.
import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
EPS = 1e-4

def oof_proba(X, y, vid, params, k=5):
    p = np.empty(len(y))
    for tr, te in GroupKFold(k).split(X, y, vid):          # cross-fitting by video
        m = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(**params).fit(X[tr], y[tr])
        p[te] = m.predict_proba(X[te])[:, 1]               # (optionally Platt-calibrate on inner folds, same for every arm)
    return np.clip(p, EPS, 1 - EPS)

def nll_bits(p, y):                                         # pointwise V-entropy -log2 f[x](y)
    return -(y * np.log2(p) + (1 - y) * np.log2(1 - p))

def cond_vinfo(X_base, X_add, y, vid, params):
    """I_V(add -> Y | base) = H_V(Y|base) - H_V(Y|base,add); returns per-row PVI-like gains."""
    h0 = nll_bits(oof_proba(X_base, y, vid, params), y)
    h1 = nll_bits(oof_proba(np.hstack([X_base, X_add]), y, vid, params), y)
    return h0 - h1                                          # mean = conditional V-information (bits/row)

def video_bootstrap(d, vid, reps=2000, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed); u = np.unique(vid)
    per = np.array([d[vid == v].mean() for v in u])          # equal weight per video, as in utility
    bs = [per[rng.integers(0, len(u), len(u))].mean() for _ in range(reps)]
    return per.mean(), np.percentile(bs, [2.5, 97.5])

def permutation_null(X_base, X_add, y, vid, params, n=100, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed); out = []
    for _ in range(n):                                      # same dimension, same marginals, link to Y broken
        Xp = X_add.copy()
        for v in np.unique(vid):
            i = np.where(vid == v)[0]; Xp[i] = X_add[rng.permutation(i)]
        out.append(cond_vinfo(X_base, Xp, y, vid, params).mean())
    return np.array(out)

def query_pvi(logit_base, logit_full, y, qid):
    """Choice-level PVI on queries with >=2 labelled candidates and one positive (softmax over candidates)."""
    res = []
    for q in np.unique(qid):
        i = np.where(qid == q)[0]
        if len(i) < 2 or y[i].sum() != 1: continue
        t = int(np.flatnonzero(y[i] == 1)[0])                                       # position of the true region
        lb = logit_base[i] - np.logaddexp.reduce(logit_base[i]); lf = logit_full[i] - np.logaddexp.reduce(logit_full[i])
        res.append(((lf[t] - lb[t]) / np.log(2),                                    # PVI_q in bits
                    int(np.argmax(logit_base[i]) == t),                              # base correct
                    int(np.argmax(logit_full[i]) == t)))                             # full correct
    return np.array(res)   # columns: pvi, base_ok, full_ok -> flips, exact McNemar on discordant pairs
 PID sketch: 
# PID on out-of-fold scores (Bertschinger/BROJA definition used by Liang et al. CVX):
# x1 = quintile bin of appearance-only logit, x2 = quintile bin of fly-only (or fly-residual-on-R1) logit, y in {0,1}.
import dit
from dit.pid import PID_BROJA
counts = np.zeros((5, 5, 2)); np.add.at(counts, (x1, x2, y), 1)
P = counts / counts.sum()
outcomes = [f"{a}{b}{c}" for a in range(5) for b in range(5) for c in range(2)]
d = dit.Distribution(outcomes, P.ravel()); d.set_rv_names("ABY")
pid = PID_BROJA(d, [[0], [1]], [2])   # redundancy, unique(A), unique(fly), synergy in bits
# repeat with x2 shuffled within video (n>=200) -> null distribution for U_fly and S; apply Miller-Madow-scale bias check
cue_role_and_regime: In the estimators the fly cue enters only as an added feature block of the probe; PID additionally tells whether its role is unique (independent evidence), redundant (same evidence as appearance) or synergistic (moderator/gate: informative only in combination, e.g. when the appearance cosine margin is small). Regimes are addressed by slicing PVI: same class and similar look (small MASA cosine margin between target and nearest neighbour), crossing paths (neighbour box overlap during loss), occlusion (loss duration), darkness/glare (eye-crop mean grey level and saturation). A positive PVI in a slice is the only form of evidence these methods give for a regime; foreign gains in other regimes say nothing about BDD100K.
no_fly_equivalent_control: Equal controls inside the information quantity: (a) R1 eye-input block of the same crop and dimension (FlyVis-specific term is I(D->Y|A,R1)); (b) stock C block (modernisation term I(D->Y|A,C)); (c) D block permuted within video (equal dimension and marginals, zero true information) as the estimator-bias null; (d) kinematic features (velocity direction, Kalman innovation, already partly in geometry) and a random projection of R1 to the D dimension; (e) for the fine-tuning upper bound, a small CNN/temporal model of similar parameter budget on the raw eye-input sequence (no connectome) evaluated by the same conditional V-information.
bio_node_mapping: The estimators are node-agnostic but can be computed per FlyVis output-type group (T4a-d, T5a-d, other columnar types, neighbour means) to locate which output types carry any unique identity information; this would point at the readout (which cell types feed identity) or, if none, at the absent lobula/LC object pathway. FlyWire 783 connectome data are not used by these methods.
novelty_overlap: Conditional V-information/conditional probing (Hewitt et al. 2021) and PID estimators (Liang et al. 2023) exist; applying them to measure what a connectome-constrained fly visual model adds to a deep appearance embedding for MOT identity was not found - the method is borrowed, only the measurement is ours.
candidate_node_change: The source implies no FlyVis change by itself; it selects which node to change: (1) if PASS-A holds and PASS-B fails (information exists but is decision-irrelevant or not exploited by concatenation) -> change the READOUT/fusion (learned fly projection added to MASA similarity with alpha starting at 0, see C01) rather than the core; (2) if Ihat(eye-input sequence -> Y|A) clearly exceeds Ihat(D->Y|A) -> core fine-tuning on identity (input preparation/dynamics/parameters) has headroom and is the candidate GPU step, because it can make existing input information usable; (3) if per-type analysis shows information only in T4/T5 under low light -> restrict the readout to those types and test that regime; (4) if all conditional quantities sit at the permutation null with a small MDE and a plateaued learning curve -> stop the identity line for the current fly input and move to another fly problem (P1-P11) or a different input preparation. Required equal controls for any follow-up: appearance only; appearance + stock C; appearance + eye input R1; appearance + equal-capacity no-fly branch; FlyVis result only if (appearance + modified fly) > (appearance + no-fly equal capacity). Condition to proceed to GPU: PASS-A and the eye-input headroom test, registered before computation.
strongest_objection: V-information is defined relative to a probe family and a finite sample: a null result with gradient boosting on 5345 rows (only 409 confusable queries, 26 video clusters on train26) cannot prove that FlyVis carries no identity information, and a positive bits gain does not have to translate into utility - our own data already show this gap (AUC +0.008 with base+D on train26 yet utility +0.106 pp with CI including 0), because extra bits may only sharpen confidence on rows where the decision does not change. The confirmation sets are reused (fit104 for selection, train26 once), so even a clean precheck is not an untouched test. And no estimator on saved features can bound what core fine-tuning would produce except through the eye-input upper bound, which itself needs a flexible estimator with the same small-sample problems.
cost_and_hardware: All CPU on saved features: one HistGradientBoosting fit on ~5k-10k rows x ~300 columns takes seconds; 5 folds x ~6 arms x (1 + 100-200 permutations) is a few thousand fits, roughly 1-4 h on 3 Idle threads [uncertain]; PID with CVX/BROJA on a 5x5x2 table takes seconds (dit or cvxpy); bootstraps negligible. The eye-input upper bound needs eye-input sequences per query (regeneration of crops may be CPU-feasible, a small CNN probe would use the 12 GB GPU for about 1-2 h) [uncertain]. No FlyVis core training is needed for the precheck.
